correctness.rationale: With row 1 as the initial label, the null-line projection on a switch multiplies squared norm by q, and a repeat leaves it unchanged. The switch bits determine each row string uniquely by recursion, so are jointly iid fair and yield the binomial law and exact mean rⁿ. The mean-normalized process is a martingale; its logarithmic drift is log(√q/r)<0, so it tends to zero and any supremum at a threshold above one is attained on this probability-one event. For the first crossing, stopped values are bounded by λ/r, so bounded-time optional stopping and dominated convergence give E[Zτ;τ<∞]=1. Equality requires no overshoot. Write A=log(1/r)>0 and B=log(r/q)>0. The finite all-up prefix through its first crossing forces log λ=mA; the finite one-down-then-up prefix forces B/A integral. Both finite prefixes have positive probability (no infinite all-up event is used). Conversely integral B/A makes +A skip-free on the lattice, so no overshoot at any level mA. Since r>√q, B/A>1; B/A=d−1 is precisely q=r^d for d≥3. Strict convexity, f_d(1/2)>0, f_d(1)=0 and f′_d(1)>0 give one nonunit root in (1/2,1), hence admissible q. Lattice rounding gives the full ceiling formula; d=3 gives the stated golden-ratio value. This argument is infinite-horizon; the frozen verifier was inspected but not executed.
residual_risks: Restricted to the fixed initialization, iid uniform sampling, and mean normalization r, not the generic operator-norm rate.

value.rationale: This supplies a concrete nonsingular randomized solver that exactly attains a time-uniform error bound, with a complete exceptional set rather than just an example. It distinguishes lattice exactness from strictness at the natural mean rate and gives a useful benchmark for adaptive error certificates. It does not assert sharpness for the different generic operator-norm rate.
residual_risks: No improvement for general matrices, noisy iterations, or other initializations is claimed.
